statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 14% and remains below the watch threshold because the session low was broken and then reclaimed, while Stress is held elevated at 56% on a 4.72% 10-year, a 30-year near 5.25% and a roughly $94 Brent risk premium.
recommendation: The mapped policy state remains EA_ON. One narrow window is flagged, 19:00Z to 20:00Z, covering the power hour on August monthly options expiry, where closing and roll flow concentrate while the long end sits near session highs. The elevated Stress reading describes cross-asset conflict rather than observed one-way Nasdaq-100 structure: the index broke to a new session low at 29,142.44 and reclaimed roughly 138 points of it, so retracements remain present in the observed price path. From 21:00Z US index futures are scheduled to halt for the weekend, so the remainder of the horizon carries a closed-market baseline.
headline: The Nasdaq-100 broke to a new session low and bought it straight back, leaving an expiry-Friday tape that is two-sided rather than one-way despite a 4.72% 10-year.
body: Cash NDX trades near 29,280.74, about +0.23% against a 29,213.17 prior close, after an opening print of 29,359.60 was faded to a 29,142.44 session low and then reclaimed by roughly 138 points; the full session range is 29,142.44 to 29,366.12. NQ September futures sit near 29,347.00, about +0.16%, against a 29,539.00 overnight high and a 29,300.50 prior close. That sequence matters more than the net change: an opening drive that failed and a downside extension that also failed is retracement-rich structure, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures. The driver remains the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMI pair, where services printed 56.8 against 54.0 expected and 54.6 prior, the strongest since December 2024, lifting the composite to 56.0 and the fastest output growth in over four years, while manufacturing slipped to a five-month low of 53.2 on Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. That mix reduces near-term easing odds: the 10-year is 4.724%, up about 2.8 basis points and near its 4.728% session high, and the 30-year trades near 5.25% after touching its highest level since 2007 earlier in the week. Against that, VIX is 15.24 and down 4.81% from a 16.01 close, which argues against a panic regime, and breadth is rotational rather than uniform, with the Dow outperforming, semiconductors the weakest tracked group in the latest session and megacap performance mixed. Brent near $94.05 and WTI near $86.69 sit on a second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 5%, with Treasury measures to isolate Iran's economy expected to be detailed on Monday. Tail is therefore eased to 14% and Stress held elevated at 56%. The remaining intraday concentration point is the 19:00Z power hour on August monthly options expiry, after which US index futures halt for the weekend from 21:00Z. The week ahead brings consumer confidence and Case-Shiller on August 25, then the GDP second estimate, July PCE and durable goods on August 26, with the Jackson Hole keynote on August 28.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: eight hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z, 11:00Z, 12:00Z, 13:00Z and 14:00Z) and the remaining sixteen clock-hours, covering the whole of the August 20 US afternoon and evening plus scattered overnight gaps, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available slots Tail stayed tightly contained between 12% and 16% with a green mapped state throughout, Stress decayed from 59% to 53% through the quiet overnight and European morning before rebuilding to 58% across the US open and the flash PMI pair, and Confidence improved steadily from 83% to 88% as more of the session's evidence became verifiable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the current hour near the post-event level while the flash PMI repricing finishes decaying, then eases gently through the New York afternoon on the assumption that price discovery stays orderly and retracements keep appearing as they have so far. One watch-level hour is carried at 19:00Z, where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow against long-end yields near session highs; expiry swings are typically two-sided and pin-driven, so the step up is deliberately narrow and single-hour. From 21:00Z US index futures are scheduled to halt for the weekend, so the final eighteen slots carry a closed-market baseline: Tail falls to 6-8% because no tradable price path exists in which mean reversion could fail, Stress sits in the moderate band reflecting weekend headline exposure through the Iran, Hormuz and oil channel ahead of Monday's Treasury announcement, and Confidence decays from 76% to 64% purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation rather than any weakening of the evidence gathered before the halt.
